speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've had this painful ulcer on your leg and have you noticed any changes in its appearance or pain level over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion's progression from a small red spot, I need to rule out pyoderma gangrenosum versus an infectious etiology. Does the ulcer have a distinct violaceous, undermined border, and have you noticed any systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of an insect bite triggering the lesion, combined with the violaceous borders and your Crohn's disease, strongly suggests pyoderma gangrenosum rather than a simple infection or venous ulcer.
